summary: Short-lived streaming fanout triggered accept-queue collapse and elevated 5xx across us-east streaming routes
description: Issue summary: Between 2026-03-12 15:10-15:35 UTC customers using short, high-frequency streaming connections experienced elevated 5xx responses from the API gateway. Impact: NimbleDocs observed ~18% of streaming sessions failing with 502/503 during a 25-minute window, causing degraded UX for real-time transcription features. Environment: Production (us-east-1), dedicated pool for NimbleDocs. Steps to reproduce: 1) Open 2000 short-lived streaming sessions (avg 3s) to /v1/stream with small payloads and immediate closure; 2) Observe upstream fanout to serving-runtime and accept-queue growth; 3) Notice increased 502/503s at API gateway and runtime restarts. Logs/metrics: accept_queue_length spiked from baseline 12 -> 240; apigw 5xx rate increased from 0.4% -> 18%; runtime process OOM kills observed on several runtimes servicing the tenant.
comments: 2026-03-12 15:20 - Aisha Mendes (Support): Customer reported "short-lived streaming calls failing intermittently"; collecting request IDs and tenant info.
2026-03-12 15:28 - NimbleDocs (Customer): We see failures primarily on quick open/close streams used by our live-caption workers. 5xx spikes last ~20m. Logs attached (request IDs: r-10f2..r-10f6).

2026-03-12 15:33 - Liam O'Connor (SRE): Observed accept_queue growth and apigw latency spikes correlating with customer session pattern. Spun up additional ephemeral proxies and temporarily increased priority shed thresholds for the tenant.
2026-03-12 15:45 - Support (Aisha): Informed customer of temporary mitigation (rate limit window and increased shed) and asked for confirmation on improvement.
2026-03-12 15:52 - NimbleDocs: Failures dropped to ~2% after mitigation; service partially recovered. We still see occasional 502s on very short streams.

2026-03-13 09:15 - Priya Shah (Runtime team): Added investigation notes to ticket; suspect rapid connect/disconnect pattern is triggering prefetch/pinning thrash and KV-cache lock contention leading to runtime OOMs.

2026-03-13 11:40 - Liam O'Connor: Added longer-term mitigations: adjust accept-queue backoff, add guardrail to limit extremely short-lived sessions per tenant, and schedule a controlled canary for the fix.
2026-03-13 12:05 - Support: Customer notified of planned fix window and asked to hold elevated sampling of their traffic during canary rollout.
investigation_notes: Correlation: apigw 5xx spike aligns with accept_queue_length and ephemeral-proxy fd usage; runtime OOMs line up with heavy prefetch and small-payload fanout patterns.

Hypothesis 1: High churn of short-lived streams causes repeated session prefills and KV cache pin/unpin thrash, causing CPU spikes and increased GC/alloc pressure in runtime leading to process restarts.
Hypothesis 2: API gateway connection pooling misheat for this tenant results in accept-queue stacking on a subset of proxies (hotspot), amplifying retry storms and hedged retries from client side.

Partial findings: NVMe / runtime I/O not saturated; however, /proc/memory fragmentation metrics show transient spikes consistent with small-allocation churn. Heap dumps from affected runtime show many ephemeral request objects at crash time.
Dashboards referenced: apigw/acceptqueue/us-east-1, runtime/kvmem/allocs, ingress/short-stream-fanout, support/tenant-NimbleDocs-traces.
Relevant logs: runtime stderr contains repeated 'kv_cache: lock contention for shard-13' entries and 'watchdog: OOM kill' around timestamps of interest.
resolution: Temporary mitigation applied: increased per-tenant short-stream gate, raised priority-shed threshold, and provisioned additional ephemeral proxies for us-east-1 to rebalance accept queues. Next steps: Runtime team to implement guardrail to coalesce very short streams (<=5s) at the gateway level to avoid fanout for backend prefills, and add KV-cache sharding fixes for lock hot shards. Scheduled canary for fix on 2026-03-16 02:00 UTC. Customer was informed and saw error rate return to acceptable levels after mitigation.
